about: The 1-minute demo video: what each scene says and shows. narration is spoken by the Windows voice ('Off Grid' is spelled for the voice); captions are shown on screen. Typos in the typed questions are deliberate and captioned as such.

scenes.narration: A typhoon hits Batangas. The power is out, and there is no internet. Most AI apps stop working here. Off Grid does not.
scenes.caption: OFFGRID: an offline emergency map and assistant for Batangas

scenes.title: 1 · Local AI on the laptop
scenes.narration: The AI runs right on this laptop: a small, three-billion-parameter model, with no cloud. It answers from saved official guides, it understands typos, and code checks every fact before you see it.
scenes.caption: Typo on purpose: “wlak thru” is read as “walk through”

scenes.title: 2 · Phones share reports through the laptop
scenes.narration: Neighbors' phones connect to the laptop over local Wi-Fi. One phone reports a flooded road, and the laptop shows it within seconds.
scenes.caption: A flooded-road report from the phone appears on the laptop map

scenes.title: 3 · Hub off: the phone keeps working
scenes.narration: Now the laptop hub is switched off. The phone still answers, even in Filipino, and gives turn-by-turn directions from its saved copy.
scenes.caption: Typo on purpose: “ospitl” is read as “ospital” (hospital)

scenes.narration: Off Grid. AI that works when the cloud doesn't. Ready beyond the grid.
scenes.caption: Local AI: Qwen 2.5 (3B) on the laptop · Phones: offline map, guides and routing (about 46 MB)

footer: Real app, recorded with the internet blocked. The phone is shown in an iPhone-sized browser window on the same laptop.
